sentences.text: This present petition is filed under Sec.166 of MV Act 1989 injured minor petitioner through his natural guardian seeking compensation of .25,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. It is the specific case of the petitioner that on 15.10.2023 at about 7.35 p.m., while he was sitting on a two-wheeler bearing registration No. KA-05-LV-595, which was parked on the service road at BB Junction from Sirsi Circle on Mysuru Road, Bengaluru, at that time the rider of a motorcycle bearing registration No. KA-05-JG-8424 (hereinafter referred to as the "offending motorcycle")
came from the "No Entry" side at a high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the parked two-wheeler.
3. Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained severe injuries all over his body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Victoria Hospital, where he was treated conservatively as an inpatient.
Thereafter, he was shifted to Manipal Hospital, where he continued treatment.
Subsequently, he was admitted to KIMS Hospital, where surgery was advised and he was treated conservatively.
It is contended that substantial amounts were incurred towards medical treatment, conveyance and other incidental expenses.
4. The petitioner contends that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle.
At the time of the accident, the petitioner was aged about 15 years and was studying in the 9th standard.
Due to the injuries sustained, he was unable to attend school and participate in curricular and extra-curricular activities, which has adversely affected his education and future prospects.

5. Hence, the petitioner has sought compensation against the respondents, being the owner and insurer of the offending motorcycle, contending that they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation along with interest for the injuries, pain and suffering, and other financial losses caused due to the accident.
6. Upon service of notice, Respondent No.1 (Owner) failed to appear before the Court and was placed ex parte.
Respondent No.2 (Insurance Company) appeared through counsel and filed its written statement denying the averments made in the petition.

While admitting the issuance of an insurance policy in respect of the offending motorcycle and that the same was valid as on the date of the accident, it has contended that its liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

7. The insurer has further contended that the owner of the offending vehicle and the concerned police authorities have failed to comply with the mandatory provisions under Section 134(c) and Section 158(6) of the Motor Vehicles Act.
It is also contended that the rider of the offending motorcycle did not possess a valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.

sentences.text: The insurance company has denied the occurrence and manner of the accident as alleged and also disputed the involvement of the offending motorcycle.

It has denied the negligence attributed to the rider of the offending motorcycle and, on the contrary, contended that the accident occurred due to the negligent parking of the two-wheeler on which the petitioner was sitting, thereby obstructing other road users.

9. Further, the insurer has denied the nature and extent of injuries, treatment taken, expenses incurred, alleged disability and quantum of compensation claimed, contending that the claim is exaggerated and exorbitant.
On these grounds, it has sought dismissal of the petition.

10. On the basis of the above, the following Issues arise for my consideration :-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent riding of motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-JG- 8424 by its rider, in RTA took place on 15-10-2023 at about 7-35 p.m., on Old Nalanda Takies,
Mysore road, Chamarajapet, Bengaluru ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
3 . What order or award?

11. In order to prove the claim, the natural guardian/father of Petitioner is examined as PW.1 and insupport of his case, 3 witnesses were examined as PW-2 to 4 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P-21.
On the other hand the Respondents have not chosen to adduce any oral and documentary evidence.

12. Heard arguments.
13.

By considering the evidences, arguments and the other materials available on record, I have answered the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative. Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:

sentences.text: 15. On the basis of the first information statement given by the petitioner, the jurisdictional police registered an FIR as per Ex.P1.
Thereafter, the police conducted spot mahazar and prepared the sketch and crime detail form as per Ex.P2.
The offending vehicle was subjected to inspection and IMV report was obtained as per Ex.P3.

After completion of investigation, the Investigating Officer filed the charge sheet against the rider of the offending motorcycle as per Ex.P5.
16.

It is also pertinent to note that the accused in C.C. No.167/2024 pleaded guilty and paid the fine amount as reflected in the order sheet marked at Ex.P6, which further strengthens the case of the petitioner regarding negligence.

17. Ex.P4 - Wound Certificate discloses that the petitioner sustained:
1. Abrasion over left forearm,
2. Abrasion over right hip,
3. Swelling over right thigh with ecchymosis and swelling and tenderness over the right side of the face.
The doctor has opined that Injury Nos.1 and 2 are simple in nature and Injury No.3 is grievous in nature.
18. On the other hand, Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company has contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the two- wheeler on which the petitioner was travelling.

During the cross-examination of PW1, it was suggested that the vehicle was parked in such a manner as to obstruct other road users and that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner's wife.
PW1 has categorically denied the said suggestions.

19. Except making such suggestions in cross- examination and taking up a defence in the written statement, Respondent No.2 has not produced any oral or documentary evidence to substantiate its contention.

No independent witness has been examined, nor any counter-investigation report or material has been placed on record to disprove the petitioner's version or to establish negligence on the part of the rider of the parked two-wheeler.

20. On careful appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence, this Tribunal finds that the testimony of PW1 is consistent, cogent and trustworthy and is duly corroborated by the contemporaneous police records.
The FIR and complaint were promptly lodged.
The IMV report indicates damage to the vehicles consistent with the manner of accident as pleaded by the petitioner.
The wound certificate and discharge summary clearly establish that the petitioner sustained grievous injury in the accident.
21. Though the insurer has disputed the occurrence and manner of the accident, it has failed to produce any credible evidence to rebut the petitioner's case.

Mere denial and bald allegations,
without substantiation, cannot outweigh the positive documentary evidence placed on record by the Mohamed Saad vs Vijay A on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197203927/

sentences.text: It is a well-settled principle that proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act are summary in nature and the standard of proof required is not as strict as in a criminal trial.

The Act is a beneficial and welfare legislation enacted to provide just and fair compensation to victims of road traffic accidents, and its provisions are to be interpreted liberally in favour of claimants.

23. Therefore, having regard to the oral and documentary evidence on record and applying the principle of beneficial construction, this Tribunal holds that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle and that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries as a result thereof.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
24. ISSUE No.2:- It is not in dispute that the petitioner was aged about 15 years at the time of the accident and was studying in the 9th standard.

The medical records disclose that he sustained grievous head injuries, namely: Right frontal and right temporal acute subdural hemorrhage (SDH),Minimal pneumocephalus, Fracture of medial wall, lateral wall and floor of the right orbit,Fracture of frontal bone,Injury to right ear and right eye.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Victoria Hospital, where he was treated as an inpatient.
Thereafter, he was shifted to Manipal Hospital and subsequently admitted to KIMS Hospital.
In all the said hospitals, he was treated conservatively and did not undergo any surgical intervention.

25. To substantiate the medical records: PW- 2, MRD of Victoria Hospital, produced the MLC extract and case sheet marked at Ex.P15 and Ex.P16. PW-3, MRO of KIMS Hospital, produced the MLC extract and inpatient records marked at Ex.P18 and Ex.P19.
26.

The petitioner further examined PW4, Dr.Bhanuprakash, Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon and Spine Surgeon, who deposed that he examined the petitioner on 07.03.2025 for the purpose of disability assessment.

PW4 stated that the petitioner had sustained right frontal-temporal fracture,
SDH, orbital fractures and contusions.

He further stated that the petitioner presently suffers from behavioral changes, irritability, memory disturbance, difficulty in concentration, giddiness, blurred vision and difficulty in performing daily activities.
Neuropsychological disability was assessed at 39.44%, and combining other components, PW4 assessed the whole body disability at 53%.
27. However, in the cross-examination, PW4 admitted:The petitioner had taken only conservative treatment and had not undergone surgery.
There was no significant vision loss.

As per Ex.P21 (Neuropsychological Assessment Report), motor speed, mental speed, focused attention, verbal working memory, visual working memory and planning response inhibition were found to be adequate.
He had not verified the school records to confirm whether the petitioner had failed or was not promoted.

28. It is also noteworthy that after discharge, the petitioner did not undergo any prolonged neuro- rehabilitation treatment nor produce follow-up records to substantiate continuing severe neurological impairment.

sentences.text: Though PW4 has assessed disability at 53% to the whole body, the same appears to be on the higher side in the absence of:Surgical intervention, Persistent neurological deficit supported by continuous treatment records, Educational records proving academic deterioration.

30. It is true that assessment of functional disability in the case of a child is inherently difficult, as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in various decisions, particularly when the injured is a non- earning minor and future prospects are uncertain.
At the same time, the Tribunal must base its assessment on objective medical evidence and surrounding circumstances.

31. Considering: The tender age of the petitioner, the nature of head injury sustained, the period of hospitalization and conservative treatment, the evidence of PW4, the absence of strong corroborative material regarding severe cognitive impairment, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the permanent physical disability to the whole body can reasonably be assessed at 25%,
instead of 53% as stated by PW4.
Accordingly, the disability is taken at 25% to the whole body for the purpose of determining just compensation.
32. There is no materials on record to establish that the Petitioner has suffered any loss to his educational career as a result of the accident.
Accordingly no compensation is awarded under the head of loss of education due to the accidental injuries.
33. As held in the Master Mallikarjuna V/s Divisional Manager reported in (2014) 14 SC 396 if the disability is above 10% and up to 30% to the whole body, the compensation should be .3 lakhs.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjuna V/s Divisional Manager reported in (2014) 14 SC 396
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For permanent disability up to 10%, it should be .1 lakh, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take a different yardstick.
In the present case whole body disability is assessed at 25%.

Considering the age of the Petitioner and nature of injuries, I deem it proper to award .3,00,000/- for Pain and sufferings already undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock, hardship,
inconvenience and discomforts, etc and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability.
34. Under the head of discomfort, inconvenience and loss of earnings to the parents during the period of hospitalization .1,00,000/- is awarded.
35. The PW1 has deposed that a sum of Rs.44,428/- incurred towards medical and incidental expenses during the period of hospitalization.
In support of this, PW1 has produced the medical bills at Ex.P.10 amounting to Rs.44,428/-.
On perusal of medical bills, it reveals that parents of the petitioner incurred the amount of Rs.44,428/- towards medical expenses.
The medical bills appear to be genuine and hence, the petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.44,428/- towards medical expenses under just and reasonable compensation.

36. By considering the above judgment, and taking into consideration of all the materials produced by the Petitioner, this tribunal awards compensation under the following heads:

Liability:
The policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence, the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the insured and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, in view of the issuance policy, the Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% per annum.
With these observations, I have answered Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
38. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioner is awarded compensation of .4,44,428/- together with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the realization.
Respondent No.2 shall pay the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of compensation amount, entire amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner in any nationalized bank till he attains the age of majority or for a period of 2 years whichever is later.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
